title: Real-time Logistics Incident Routing
business: Global logistics providers managing millions of shipment status updates per hour.
problem: Legacy rule-based systems fail to categorize unstructured delivery exceptions, leading to manual triage bottlenecks and delayed customer notifications.
solution: Deploying Claude Haiku 5.5 to perform high-volume, latency-sensitive classification of incoming shipment logs, automatically routing them to the appropriate regional resolution teams.
steps: Ingest raw shipment log streams into a high-throughput message queue.
Invoke the claude-haiku-5-5 model via the API for each log entry to classify the exception type.
Utilize the adaptive thinking capability with the effort parameter set to low to minimize latency for routine classifications.
Route the classified output to the specific downstream resolution service based on the model's structured JSON response.
outcome: Significant reduction in manual triage time and improved accuracy in routing complex delivery exceptions to specialized support staff.
limitation: The model's adaptive thinking depth is controlled by the effort parameter; setting it too low for highly ambiguous logs may result in classification errors, requiring a tradeoff between speed and reasoning depth.
